evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 10.16 mg/L at t=239 h vs 1.39 mg/L at t=240 h — an instantaneous step collapse of ~8.8 mg/L within one 0.2 h sampling interval
Receiving DO2 remains pinned at 0.9–1.6 mg/L from t=240 to t=259 h, below the 2 mg/L hard limit, so KEEP is infeasible
Source batches 1–3 show similar but milder DO dips (~13 to ~8 mg/L near t≈119 h) that recover, supporting a transient load-step mechanism responsive to feed reduction
allowed_actions: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air], retaining more feed than strong_feed_reduction [0.6, 1.15] while adding transfer headroom
Online sensor rows available at 259 h; last assay: product P = 2.92 g/L at t=239 h (avail 259 h)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO collapsed stepwise from 10.16 mg/L (t=239 h) to ~1.4 mg/L (t=240 h) and has stayed at 0.9–1.6 mg/L through the latest reading — a hard violation of the 2 mg/L limit that KEEP would perpetuate. The instantaneous step (one 0.2 h sampling interval) points to a sudden oxygen-demand load (feed-driven) rather than gradual transfer-capacity decay; the three source batches show the same signature in milder form (~13→8 mg/L dips near t≈119 h) that recovers, corroborating a load-step mechanism. Scaling the ~8.8 mg/L demand spike: reduce_feed (0.8×) leaves ~7.0 mg/L of spike, giving DO ≈ 10.2 − 7.0 ≈ 3.1 mg/L, and the 1.15× air factor adds ~0.4–0.5 mg/L transfer headroom, so combined is centrally predicted at ~3.5 mg/L — above the limit with ~1.5 mg/L margin — while retaining 80% feed (more product than strong_feed_reduction). increase_air alone (~1.4–2.4 mg/L central) is too marginal; strong_feed_reduction wastes product mass; stop discards all product despite a supported feasible plan. No extra assay requested because the process continues under KEEP (violating) during the 4 h assay turnaround.
submission.uncertainty: The feed-proportional load model is inferred from the step shape and source-batch analogy, not from a calibrated physics tool; if the collapse were instead a large kLa/aeration failure, feed cuts relieve only the baseline OUR and combined might remain near or below 2 mg/L. Forecast error of ±1 mg/L is plausible; combined's central margin (~1.5 mg/L above the limit) covers moderate error, but strong_feed_reduction would be the fallback if the constraint were later still violated. Product-mass trade-off of strong_feed_reduction (~20% further feed cut) was not taken because central prediction shows it unnecessary.
